name: Hariom Pipe Industries Ltd
title: Hariom Pipe Industries Ltd - 543517 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 volume growth fell short of the 30% guided last quarter; management now guides FY27 volume of 350,000–360,000 t (~20–25%) with blended EBITDA/t near ₹7,200–7,800 and no firm margin target. Capacity is not the constraint, and the Perundurai closure is a freight and sourcing issue.

summary.headline: Hariom Pipe FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR1,667 crore and EBITDA 19% to INR209 crore at a 12.56% margin, with FY27 volume guided at 350,000-360,000 tonnes.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,667 crore (+23% YoY), EBITDA INR209 crore (+19%) and PAT INR76 crore (+23%), with EBITDA margin broadly stable at 12.56%. Q4 revenue was INR507 crore (+27% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR64 crore (+31%) and Q4 PAT INR30 crore (+75%). FY26 volume growth fell short of the 30% guided last year, as management prioritised margin and cash over volume. Management said a Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closure linked to a pollution board order had not yet hit volumes, citing stock and asset-light supply, and that reopening was expected within days.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to EBITDA / ROCE / ROE (FY26)

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Management stated value-added products were 98% of FY26 revenue (analyst cited about 90% earlier). Galvanised products were described as a meaningful contributor.

segments.name: B2B / OEM channel
segments.commentary: B2B share of sales rose to about 20% in Q4 FY26 from about 15% earlier, per management. Management said the target is to add more OEM and engineering clients.

segments.name: Renewable energy (Hariom Power & Energy, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 60 MW AC solar project under MSEDCL PPA across 13 locations; 8 locations taken up, about 38 MW under work, and about 10 MW expected to start production next month. Investment to date INR9.56 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guided at about 350,000-360,000 tonnes, roughly 20-25% growth on FY26 (about 288,000 tonnes), subject to market conditions; management said 30% growth is possible on existing capacity but not at the cost of margins.
No firm EBITDA per tonne number for FY27; management said the current level (about INR7,200-7,800 blended) is the minimum to sustain, with no percentage growth target given.

Solar: 60 MW project to be completed within FY27; project cost about INR241-245 crore, bank term loan about INR195 crore, equity from Hariom Pipes about INR25-30 crore, balance expected from central capital subsidy; FY27 solar revenue to be quantified at Q1 results.
Backward integration rising from about 40% to about 80% depends on an environmental clearance from the Government of India; management said 3-4 months after approval, with no assured timeline.
Q1 FY27 current trading described as good; management declined to give a specific Q1 YoY volume growth number.
capex_capacity: 60 MW AC solar project (subsidiary Hariom Power & Energy) under MSEDCL PPA; 13 locations, 8 taken up, 2 yet to commence, rest targeted in FY27; land of about 123 acres acquired at 8 locations and work started at 6.
Solar tariff about INR3.21 per unit plus central capital subsidy; fixed-tenure revenue.
Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closed on a pollution board order; management said pile was moved, compliances completed, and reopening order awaited within 2-3 working days.
Backward integration at about 40%; expansion to about 80% requires a pending EC order.
Metal Mart Private Limited incorporated for metals trading, still at initial setup; GST registrations in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana in progress.
demand_pricing: Management said the market is competitive and steel prices are volatile; EBITDA per tonne is driven by market demand and supply, not MRP.
Scaffolding demand weak in FY26 because the business is credit-based; management said it is not extending the credit needed to push volume.

Management said dealer losses from the Perundurai closure were nil, with some dealers buying from competitors for a short period; the company supplied commercial products to Kerala from stock and other facilities.
Gas supply disruption: management said there was no impact in Q4, with own suppliers and storage in place.
Analyst's view: EBITDA per tonne can mislead when prices rise; management did not commit to a per-tonne target.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still stand by 30% FY27 volume growth guidance, and what EBITDA per tonne is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capacity for about 30% growth on about 288,000 tonnes, subject to market conditions and no compromise on margins. Blended EBITDA is about INR7,200 per tonne, and management said it is confident of maintaining that level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu plant open, and what revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant awaits a reopening order within 2-3 working days, and April 2026 turnover matched April 2025 because of stock and asset-light supply. It said no non-compliance was found and that the closure followed election-period actions by the authorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar capex, debt and revenue roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Total project cost is about INR241 crore with INR195 crore bank debt and an equity component of INR25-30 crore; INR9.56 crore is invested so far. Management said the remainder is backed by central capital subsidy and that solar revenue will be quantified at Q1 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne or margin be the better guidance metric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins of about 12.5-12.6% are sustainable and it focuses on profitability rather than volume. It said the EBITDA per tonne figure is not price-dependent in a fixed way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B share and the FY27 product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B was about 20% of sales in Q4, up from 15%. Management said the mix is coils across MS and GI, the focus is B2B plus dealers, and dealer addition is continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Metal Mart subsidiary have a start date?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supplier tie-ups are done and GST registrations are pending in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, with operations to start once registrations are received.

risks_watch: Tamil Nadu plant reopening timing and any Q1 volume impact; the stated April turnover parity relies on stock and third-party supply.
Volume delivery against the 350,000-360,000 tonne guide, given FY26 undershot the earlier 30% growth guide and scaffolding demand is weak.
Steel price volatility and input cost swings (gas, power, logistics) that management said can affect EBITDA per tonne.
Solar project execution: remaining 2 locations to start, FY27 completion, subsidy realisation and ~INR160 crore net debt rising in FY27 with depreciation and interest impact.
EC clearance for backward integration (40% to 80%), with no assured timing.
Management commentary on the Tamil Nadu closure cause was not fully clear and drew follow-up questions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and cash, but evasive on volume and the Tamil Nadu closure: management declined to reaffirm the 30% growth guide, gave no firm EBITDA per tonne target, and avoided Q1 volume numbers. Several answers were disjointed on the closure reason.
key_quotes: Our area is not the volume, our area is always the profitability.
We will continue to focus on profitable growth rather than only volume-led growth.
EBITDA margins are sustainable, basically, whatever is being shown in the numbers are there.

adds.what: 60 MW AC solar project (Hariom Power & Energy subsidiary) under MSEDCL PPA; about 10 MW expected to start production next month
Backward integration expansion from about 40% to about 80%, pending a government environmental clearance (EC) order

growth.why: FY27 volume guided at 350,000-360,000 t (about 20-25% growth on about 288,000 t), with management saying 30% is possible on existing capacity; backing is partial, as the solar project and the EC-dependent backward integration are the only specific capacity items, and no volume-level order book was given.
